correctness.rationale: Direct forest and unsigned Stirling-number counting reconstructs the exact law for all n; exceptional equal cycles are separately normalized. Gaussian product bounds and singularity-integrable Riemann sums prove both the macroscopic intensity and all fixed q>0 moment constants; exact integral of the intensity yields the tail. Independent exact map enumeration n=2..6 verifies every finite stratum, and exact finite moment formulas corroborate asymptotic normalization without being treated as proof.

value.rationale: A natural conditioned component order statistic exhibits a nontrivial and quantified failure of uniform integrability: typical shorter cycle n^U with U uniform in (0,1/2), but any fixed positive power moment is dominated by rare cycles on sqrt(n) scale. The locally finite macroscopic intensity and exact tail/moment constants identify this boundary for a meaningful class of order statistics, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
